evidence.label: def:p15-exchangeable-canonical: canonical space, E_n, E, T, exchangeability, I_{n,k}, (n)_k, A_{n,k} (definitions and hypotheses present)
def:p15-permutable-events: the retained finite permutations T_pi
properties of the defined fields proved in annex:p15.exchangeable-canonical

components.gap: Worked boundary not supplied. The definitions and hypotheses are present (body 15-43, with T_pi retained from limsup 194-212), and Durrett's E_n/E and exchangeability definitions (pp. 250, 253) and Feller's finite/infinite definition (VII.4, p. 228) are preserved. But neither the entry nor any on-route text tied to it works a boundary case of the defined notions: no law shown not to be exchangeable, no case with E_{n+1} strictly inside E_n or T strictly inside E, no edge of A_{n,k}. 'Each permutation in this formula fixes every coordinate beyond n' and 'These are exact invariant-event definitions' are clarifications, not a worked boundary. No reason is given for the field being inapplicable. The non-exchangeable chain and trend in the 163.10 chapter (w02b-p15-022 body 252-269) belong to that chapter's own component and are not tied to this entry.

evidence.label: thm:p15-exchangeable-canonical statement
annex:p15.exchangeable-canonical: written proof of the equivalence, sigma-field, decrease, T in E and pull-back reduction

components.gap: Worked boundary not supplied. The statement (body 45-55) and every step of the declared annex proof (annex 4-36) are present, covering the equivalence in both directions, the sigma-field, the decrease, T contained in E, and the pull-back reduction. No boundary case is worked anywhere for this lemma: no example where the inclusion T in E or E_{n+1} in E_n is strict, and no case showing what the canonical reduction does not give. The proof's last sentence (annex 34-35) only states a scope limitation. The strict-inclusion material of the limsup chapter belongs to that unit's own components and is not tied to this entry.

components.gap: Worked boundary not supplied. The statement (body 57-68) and the written proof (annex 39-62) are complete. The proof keeps Durrett's computation (p. 252, Lemma 4.7.7; p. 253, Theorem 4.7.9 proof) and extends it from bounded to integrable phi. But neither the integrability hypothesis nor the per-integrand null-set limitation is worked at its boundary. 'Different integrands may have different exceptional null sets' (body 67) is an unworked caveat, and 'No boundedness is needed' (annex 60-61) restates the hypothesis. The only worked integrability failure on the route, infinite-mean i.i.d. averages (w02b-p15-022 body 904-906, annex 348-364), is presented as the boundary of thm:p15-reverse-strong-law and is not tied to this entry.

def:p15-directing-law: P(S), evaluation sigma-field, countable determining pi-system, kernel, Lambda, sigma(K), G^P
construction of the determining class and generation of the evaluation sigma-field
G^P is a sigma-field containing null events

components.gap: Worked boundary not supplied. The definitions are present (body 154-174). The construction of the countable determining class and of its generating role is written (annex 291-299), and G^P is shown to be a sigma-field (annex 310-313). No boundary of these notions is worked: no example where G^P is strictly larger than G, and no case showing where the standard Borel hypothesis is needed for the determining class or kernel. 'This records equality of information modulo ambient measurable null events' (body 172) is a clarification. The arbitrary-space P(S) and the point-mass example of the 163.10 chapter (w02b-p15-022 body 1028-1046, 1085-1102) belong to the presentability boundary, not to this definition.

C014 annex: the closing uniqueness paragraph relies on 'the measurable-section strong-law argument used for the Polya mixture'. That argument is written in thm:p15-polya-mixture-representation only for a beta parameter law, so for a general lambda this step is invoked by reference, not written. It lies outside the entry's stated existence claim, so it was not scored against C014.

C006: the body (line 104) says the source Example 4.7.4 argument is preserved. Durrett (p. 251) obtains triviality of E from his Theorem 2.5.4, while the annex uses the reverse-average Hewitt--Savage theorem of this chapter. The conclusion is the same, but this substitution of the zero-one input is not flagged as a variant.
